record.original_question: Can one make progress in counting the number of fixed points by studying the spectrum of the quantisation of mu: M → S1? This type of problem should be very relevant to the study of equilibriu m points of integrable systems but, for the moment, it is only a toy version to start with. The gener al case would involve quantisation and a study of the fixed point properties of an object (momentum m ap) of the form M → (S1)k × Rn, and this will likely be quite challenging. 7.3 Quantum integrability for polynomial in momenta integr als The approach to quantisation of natural Hamiltonian systems discu ssed in this section is, perhaps, the most traditional. Instead of a Hamiltonian of the form (3.1), i.e., H = K + U on a Riemannian manifold M, one considers the second order differential operator acting on C2-differentiable functions on M and given by ˆH:= ∆ + U, where ∆ = gij∇ i∇ j is the Beltrami-Laplace operator corresponding to g. Next, by a quantum integral we understand another differential operator ˆF that commutes with H: [ ˆH, ˆF ] = ˆH ◦ ˆF - ˆF ◦ ˆH = 0. (7.1) Sometimes one requires that the operator ˆF be self-adjoint. It is known and is easy to see that, for any operators ˆH and ˆF, the symbol of [ ˆH, ˆF ] is just the Poisson bracket of the symbols of ˆH and ˆF. We say that a polynomial in momenta integral F for (3.1) is quantisable if there exists a quantum integral ˆF for ˆH such that its symbol is F.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact connected symplectic manifold equipped with a Hamiltonian circle action whose momentum map is $\mu : M \to S^1$ (regarded as an $S^1$-valued Hamiltonian). The fixed point set of the $S^1$-action coincides with the set of critical points of $\mu$. Suppose one constructs a quantization of $\mu$, i.e.\ a self-adjoint operator $\widehat{\mu}$ acting on a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ associated with $(M,\omega)$ via a chosen quantization scheme (e.g.\ geometric or Berezin–Toeplitz quantization), whose principal symbol is $\mu$.

Question: Can one extract information about, and in particular count, the number of fixed points of the $S^1$-action on $M$ purely from spectral data of $\widehat{\mu}$ (such as its eigenvalues, their asymptotic distribution, or associated semiclassical invariants)?

More generally, given a Hamiltonian action of $T^k \times \mathbb{R}^n$ on $(M,\omega)$ with momentum map $\mu : M \to (S^1)^k \times \mathbb{R}^n$ and an appropriate joint quantization $\widehat{\mu}$, determine to what extent the spectrum (joint spectrum) of $\widehat{\mu}$ recovers the fixed point structure (number, indices, and local invariants of fixed points) of the underlying classical action, providing in particular a method to count equilibrium points of the corresponding integrable system.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a numbered open problem in a 2018 collection on open problems in finite-dimensional integrable systems and is attributed to A. Pelayo. No published resolution counting fixed points via the spectrum of the quantization of an $S^1$-valued momentum map (let alone the general $(S^1)^k \times \mathbb R^n$ case) was found; related work on inverse spectral theory for semitoric and toric integrable systems by Pelayo–Vũ Ngọc and collaborators addresses adjacent questions but does not appear to settle this counting problem.

status_evidence.snippet: Pelayo and Vũ Ngọc study how spectral data of quantum integrable systems determine classical invariants.
